text:
maria-enginfra: heads up — after the kernel roll in us-west2 this morning we're seeing A100 nodes report P2P as disabled and BAR1 window sizes reduced. Jobs failing with NCCL timeouts. anyone else seeing this?
lee-sre: saw similar telemetry in eu-west1 around 06:12 UTC, but only a subset of instances. driver version 535.98 + kernel 5.15.0-rc1.
aj-mlinfra: confirm — several reduce-scatter jobs get stuck at startup, logs show failed cuDeviceGetP2PAttribute or returns 0 for P2P capability. NCCL reports "incompatible topologies".
ops-oncall: paging spike from batch inference queue, SLA breaches on 3 customer pods. redirecting traffic to us-east1 as a temp measure. :rotating_light:
deploy-bot: rollout-api: kernel/driver rollout completed on 44 hosts, 14 hosts remaining.
nina-platform: what's the scope? single AZ or entire region? affects autoscaler decisions if BAR1 is mis-sized.
maria-enginfra: mostly us-west2-a and b so far, but a few hosts in c show degraded BAR1 ads too. looks like BAR1 aperture reported as 256MB instead of 1GB on some nodes.
sam-neteng: PCIe ACS changes in the kernel can flip BAR mapping and inter-device visibility. vendor notes mention ACS override behavior changed in this kernel patch.
lee-sre: immediate mitigation idea — boot with pcie_acs_override=downstream to force ACS behavior back, or use kernel cmdline to disable the aggressive ACS enforcement. risky but cheap to try on a canary host.
aj-mlinfra: testing suggestion: spin up a small NCCL multi-GPU job with --reduce-scatter and check p2p status via nvidia-smi topo --matrix and /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/p2p_status.
maria-enginfra: tried on a single host, setting pcie_acs_override=downstream recovered P2P and BAR1 reports went back to expected size, NCCL job completed. need approval to push to a 5-node canary.
ops-oncall: approve canary. but we need an ops playbook entry in case rollback required. log all kernel cmdline changes to host metadata.
nina-platform: cost note — moving inference load to other regions is adding ~18% hourly spend on GPUs, heading into reserved-capacity risk if prolonged. ops-oncall: acknowledged.
sam-neteng: long-term fix is vendor driver/kernel combo that preserves BAR1 aperture and P2P semantics; filing ticket with vendor and backport tree.
maria-enginfra: creating canary now, will post results. for anyone triaging, sample diagnostic commands: ```sh
nvidia-smi topo --matrix
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/p2p_status
dmesg | grep -i acs
```
lee-sre: also capture lspci -vv output for affected host (look for ACS: Reported and ACS: Enabled flags).
aj-mlinfra: adding synthetic eval to catch this class of regression: small NCCL transfer test in our CI for driver/kernel upgrades.
ops-oncall: canary results in 15m? set alert to unmute for me.
deploy-bot: canary-group: kernel-cmdline-pcie-acs applied to host-045, host-046, host-052, host-053, host-061.
maria-enginfra: canary passed — P2P restored on 5/5, BAR1 aperture back to 1GB, NCCL jobs succeeded. planning staged rollout for remaining affected hosts with 10-host batches and 30m observation windows.
sam-neteng: add network-level health checks for p2p latency (iperf between GPUs) and include in console dashboard.
nina-platform: schedule meeting with vendor + maintainers to get upstream patch; raise MR to pin safe kernel in our dedicated pools until vendor fix is available.
lee-sre: follow-up: produce a short postmortem once rollout completes, include cost delta from regional spillover, and the kernel cmdline diff applied.
ops-oncall: update oncall runbook to include this quick ACS toggle and the canary checklist. :white_check_mark:
maria-enginfra: thanks team — I'll write the rollout runbook and add the diagnostic snippets to the eng-infra wiki. will update thread with any regressions during the staged rollout.
